1955.name: Texas Weekly Cattle Auction Summary
1955.narrative: Compared to last week:  Steer and heifer calves sold mostly 5.00 to 15.00 higher, with the largest advances noted on weaned cattle carrying at least two rounds of vaccinations. Significant discounts were once again noted on unweaned cattle, as recent weather conditions have contributed to increased health concerns among those calves. Winter grazing prospects remain promising, with 82 percent of the Texas winter wheat crop planted and 71 percent emerged, compared to the five-year average of 63 percent, according to USDA-NASS. Additionally, 42 percent of the crop is rated in good to excellent condition, providing further support for wheat grazing demand through the winter months.

3724.name: Giddings Livestock Auction - Giddings, TX
3724.narrative: Total receipts were 856 compared to 595 last week. Rainfall in the area led to a lower number of cattle again this week.  Feeder steers under 500 lbs. were 12.00 to 24.00 higher.  Feeder steers over 500 lbs. were 12.00 to 16.00 higher.  Feeder heifers under 500 lbs. were 10.00 to 17.00 higher.  Feeder heifers over 500 lbs. were 8.00 to 10.00 higher.  Slaughter cows were 2.00 to 4.00 lower.  Slaughter bulls were steady on a very limited test.

2015.name: Producers Livestock Cattle Auction - San Angelo, TX
2015.narrative: Compared to last week, feeder cattle overall sold on a light test due lighter receipts last week, however a higher undertone was noted. Slaughter cows sold 4.00 to 5.00 lower. Slaughter bulls sold 2.00 to 3.00 lower.

2014.name: Producers Livestock Sheep and Goat Auction - San Angelo, TX
2014.narrative: Compared to last week, slaughter lambs sold 16.00 to sharply lower, while ewes traded softer. Feeder kids sold 8.00 higher, while slaughter kids traded 6.00 to sharply lower. Next report release will be December 2, 2026.
